entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya releases the first 20 Ebola contacts from quarantine
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry released the first 20 contacts after 21 days of monitoring without symptoms. Health Director-General Patrick Amoth said the outbreak is not over; the remaining 98 contacts are expected to leave quarantine in four waves from 3 November, based on individual health assessments, Reuters reported.
entry.content:

Sources: Reuters via KSL, Capital FM

ECDC's update of 25 October, covering data to 24 October, counted 9,964 cases and 4,851 deaths.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: First participant vaccinated in the Tumaini trial
entry.summary: CEPI said the first participant was vaccinated on 23 October in Bunia, DR Congo, marking the start of Tumaini, a pivotal Phase 2/3 trial of vaccine candidates against Bundibugyo virus run with Epicentre, MSF, WHO and Africa CDC. Bloomberg reported that the first dose was Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire species; whether it protects against Bundibugyo is not yet known. Experimental candidates from Moderna and from Oxford with the Serum Institute of India could be added within weeks, Bloomberg reported.

Kenya's health ministry has said all nine of its cases belong to one cluster; Nigeria has placed 44 contacts under follow-up.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: CDC requires an Ebola attestation for all US-bound air passengers
entry.summary: CDC issued an order requiring every passenger boarding an international flight to the United States, whatever their nationality, to attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the 21 days before boarding. The requirement starts at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November, and airlines must check the attestation before boarding. It adds to CDC's existing entry restrictions for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.
entry.content:

The requirement starts at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November, and airlines must check the attestation before boarding. It adds to CDC's existing entry restrictions for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

Sources: CDC order, NBC News, CNBC Africa (Reuters)

Reuters and Al Jazeera report that CDC confirmed it after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate. CDC has not said where the death occurred and says its count could change as reviews continue. Pennsylvania's own count is five.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said one more person tested positive, bringing the total to nine including the first patient, who died. The new case is a contact of the first patient who was already in quarantine. The ministry said all nine cases belong to one cluster, that there is no evidence of transmission outside it, and that 134 of 135 identified contacts were in quarantine. It said the first group of contacts completes 21 days of quarantine on 25 October.

entry.title: Ebola · DR Congo: Nigeria confirms an imported Ebola case
entry.summary: Nigeria's health ministry confirmed one case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, in a person with recent travel to Uganda; laboratory confirmation was on 20 October. Officials said 44 contacts had been identified. WHO calls it an imported case and the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak was declared, says where and when the person was exposed is not yet known, and advises against restrictions on travel or trade.

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: Southern Nevada reports its first clade I mpox case
entry.summary: The Southern Nevada Health District reported the first confirmed clade I mpox case in a Clark County resident. The district said the person has no reported travel exposure, so the source of infection is unclear, and that it has reported 11 clade II cases since August. It said anyone who may have been exposed should contact a health care provider and watch for symptoms for 21 days, and that JYNNEOS vaccine is expected to protect against both clades.

entry.title: Cholera · Global: Zambia declares a new cholera outbreak and starts oral vaccination

It is separate from the outbreak the government declared over in July. On 17 October the health ministry's figures, reported by Lusaka Times and Xinhua, were 966 cases and 25 deaths in 12 districts across five provinces, as the country launched an oral cholera vaccination campaign in Lusaka and Chibombo district.

entry.title: Cholera · Global: WHO: suspected cholera cases in Yemen roughly triple in three weeks
entry.summary: WHO says Yemen has recorded 8,034 suspected cholera cases and 27 deaths so far this year, and that weekly cases roughly tripled over three weeks. Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people (Abyan, Lahij, Al Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden) account for 92% of reported cases. WHO called for funding and access to safe water, vaccination and health services.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
entry.summary: Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
entry.summary: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".
